The TSH receptor (TSHR) gene mutation p.S425l was found at an allelic frequency of 13%. Somatic mutations of TSHR are known to frequently occur in autonomously functioning thyroid nodules (AFTN). Although infrequent, p.S425l has been reported in the Cosmic database. Rare cases of thyroid cancer in hyperfunctioning nodules with TSHR mutations have been reported and were also seen in our validation series, but in those cases the mutation was found with an allelic frequency of >30%
NRAS mutation was also identified in this sample at a low level with an allelic frequency of 4% which corresponds to a heterozygous mutation present in 8% of cells. The finding of this mutation at a LOW LEVEL, as in this case, is likely due to a clone within the nodule, with potential for expansion and progression in some but not all cases. Therefore, the risk of cancer in this nodule at present time is likely to be low. Correlation of the molecular findings with clinical data and possibly repeat FNA in 6-12 months or at another time interval to assess the potential cytological and molecular progression of the mutant clone could be recommended, if clinically indicated.
